source_text: 17 DE AMMUDATE ET DEO MAGNO. Diximus iam multa de superstitione nefanda, Et tamen exsequimur, ne quod praeterisse dicamur. Ammudatem qui suum cultores more colebant, Magnus erat illis, quando fuit aurum in aedem. Mittebant capita sub numine quasi praesenti. Uentum est ad summum, ut Caesar tolleret aurum: Deficit numen aut fugit aut transit in ignem. Auctor huius sceleris constat, qui formabat eundem. Tot uiros et magnos seduxit false prophetans, Et modo retacuit qui solebat esse diuinus. Erumpebat enim uocis quasi mente mutata, Tamquam illi deus ligni loqueretur in aurem. Dicite nunc ipsi, si non sunt numina falsa. Ex eo prodigio, quod perdidit, ille propheta Oblitus est iste prophetare, qui ante solebat. Monstra deo ista fincta sunt per uiniuoraces, Audacia quorum damnabilis numina fingit. Gestabantur enim, et aliut tale sigillum: Nunc et ipse silet, nec ullus de illo prophetat. O nimium <stulti>, sed uos ipsos perdere uultis.
pass_a_gloss: Ammudas magnus dum aurum in aede. Caesar tollit aurum — numen deficit. False prophetans seduxit; now retacet. Deus ligni in aurem. Numina falsa — uos perdere uultis.
pass_b_english: We have already said much of unspeakable superstition, and still we pursue it lest we be said to have skipped something. Ammudas, whom his worshipers used to cultivate in their fashion — he was great for them when there was gold in the temple. They put their heads under the divinity as if present. It came to the summit that Caesar took the gold: the divinity fails or flees or passes into fire. The author of this crime stands clear — he who was shaping the same. He seduced so many and great men, falsely prophesying, and now he has fallen silent who used to be divine. For a voice used to burst out as if with altered mind, as though a god of wood spoke into his ear. Say now yourselves if the divinities are not false. From that prodigy which he lost, that prophet forgot to prophesy who before used to. Those monsters are feigned for a god by the devourers of wine, whose damnable boldness fashions divinities. For they were carried about, and another such little image: now he himself is silent, nor does anyone prophesy of him. O too much fools — but you want to destroy yourselves.

choices.choose: see gold-god fail when gold is taken

choices.reject: trust wood speaking in the ear

choices.why: si non sunt numina falsa; uos… perdere
